alignment.twoThingsYouWantThat: Two things you want that pull apart

alignment.step6OfTheJourney: Step 6 of the journey. It lays your goals next to the career areas you picked and next to how you're actually built, and says plainly where those three agree and where they don't.
alignment.someOfWhatYouWant: Some of what you want will come easily to you. Some of it will take more out of you than it takes out of other people. That's worth knowing before you build a plan on top of it — not so you drop the hard thing, but so you go in with your eyes open and some support in place.
alignment.whereTwoOfYourGoals: Where two of your goals genuinely pull against each other, this step says so instead of smoothing it over. A tension is information about a trade-off, not a judgement about you, and nothing here is a score.

alignment.weCouldnTCheckWhether: We couldn't check whether you've already run this — that's a fault on our side, not a sign there's nothing here. Running it again is safe either way.
alignment.thisOneIsComputedRather: This one is computed rather than stored, so it has to be asked for. It reads your goals and your behavioural profile and takes a little while — long enough that we hand it off and come back for it.
alignment.youCanRunItNow: You can run it now whatever state those two steps are in. It will tell you what it was missing rather than pretend it wasn't.
alignment.belowIsYourMostRecent: Below is your most recent completed run.
alignment.worthDoingAfterYouChange: Worth doing after you change your goals or take a new assessment. Nothing else about this reads differently.

goals.step5OfTheJourney: Step 5 of the journey. This is a conversation, not a form — you talk it through with Goals Studio over as many sittings as you need, and it keeps everything between visits.
goals.yourGoalsLiveInOne: Your goals live in one place
goals.theInterviewYourDraftsPublishing: The interview, your drafts, publishing and who can see them are all at My Goals. This step is done when you have confirmed a goal there — the map picks that up when you come back.
goals.theGoalsYouHaveSo: The goals you have so far
goals.goalsWithTheReasonUnderneath: Goals with the reason underneath them
goals.mostGoalSettingStopsAt: Most goal-setting stops at the first answer, which is why most goals don't survive a bad week. Goals Studio keeps asking why — up to five times, and no further — until it reaches something you actually care about rather than something you think you should say. That root is what everything after this step gets aimed at.
goals.weCouldnTReadYour: We couldn't read your progress just now, so this step may show as not started. Your goals themselves are unaffected.

interview.whatTheyReMostLikely: What they're most likely to dig into
interview.theseComeFromThePlaces: These come from the places where your profile sits furthest from what this role is benchmarked for. Being asked about them isn't a trap — it's the part of the conversation you can prepare for.
interview.whereTheConversationMightGet: Where the conversation might get uncomfortable
interview.everyoneHasHabitsThatShow: Everyone has habits that show up under pressure. Interviewers probe them because they're normal, not because something is wrong with you. Having an honest example ready takes the sting out.
interview.questionsThatComeUpFor: Questions that come up for almost any role
interview.interviewsFeelLikeATest: Interviews feel like a test of who you are. They're mostly a test of how well you've thought about it beforehand — and that part is entirely within your control. This page tells you which questions this particular role is likely to lean on, and why.
interview.lookingUpTheRolesYou: Looking up the roles you're matched to…
interview.thereSNoRoleTo: There's no role to prepare for yet.
interview.theQuestionsOnThisPage: The questions on this page are built from one specific role's benchmark compared with your own profile — that's what makes them worth rehearsing rather than generic. So we need a target role first, and that comes from your job matches. If your matches are empty, it usually means no roles have been published to you yet, which is normal early on and isn't anything you did wrong.
interview.whichRoleAreYouPreparing: Which role are you preparing for?
interview.builtFromYourProfile: Built from your profile against this role's benchmark. Rebuild it any time your profile changes.
interview.wellWorkOutTheQuestions: We'll work out the questions this role is likely to lean on for you specifically.
interview.thatDidnTComeBack: That didn't come back just now. Try again in a moment — nothing has been lost.
interview.wantToPractiseSayingAny: Want to practise saying any of this out loud?

matches.thereArenTAnyRoles: There aren't any roles to compare you with yet
matches.ifYouReNotAttached: If you're not attached to an employer here, the shared library is all there is — and it's still being built. Every benchmark in it is read and checked by a person before it's published, and that work isn't finished, so right now there's nothing on the other side of the comparison.
matches.nothingIsMissingFromYour: Nothing is missing from your profile, and nothing has gone wrong. When the first benchmarks are published, your matches will appear here on their own — you won't have to redo anything.
matches.inTheMeantimeTheseDo: In the meantime, these do work:
matches.roleMatchingIsSwitchedOff: Role matching is switched off for now
matches.weVePausedThisStep: We've paused this step while the matching is checked over. It's a deliberate hold, not a fault at your end and nothing to do with your profile — it'll come back on without you doing anything.
matches.everythingElseInYourJourney: Everything else in your journey is unaffected, and anything you finish now feeds straight into your matches the moment they're back.
matches.thisGatesJobMatchesAnd: This gates Job Matches, and Job Matches gates My Plan and Interview Prep — so all three come back together.
matches.savedTargetIs: Your saved target role is {{role}}. Pick another role to change it.
matches.savedTargetNotInListNamed: Your saved target role, {{role}}, isn't in this list right now. It stays your target unless you pick a role here.
matches.savedTargetNotInListUnnamed: Your saved target role isn't in this list right now. It stays your target unless you pick a role here.
matches.savedTargetUnnamed: You already have a target role saved. It stays your target unless you pick a role here.
matches.whichRolesSuitTheWay: Which roles suit the way you're actually wired, and how far you are from each one. Pick a role to see where you already match it and where there's ground to make up.
matches.liningYourProfileUpAgainst: Lining your profile up against published roles…
matches.weCouldnTLoadYour: We couldn't load your matches just now. Refresh to try again — nothing you've done has been lost.
matches.workingOutWhereYouStand: Working out where you stand against this role…
matches.weCouldnTOpenThe: We couldn't open the breakdown for this role. Pick another, or try again in a moment.
matches.stepLinesUpAgainst: This step lines your profile up against <1>published role benchmarks</1> — the detailed profiles of what a role actually asks for. Those come from two places: an employer's own library, and a shared library that's open to everyone.
matches.turningItOnNote: Matching is always computed — this flag only controls who can see it. Set <1>BLUEPRINT_MATCHING_ENABLED=true</1> on the blueprint-service Lambda via CDK (<3>-c blueprintMatching=true</3>), not by editing the Lambda directly — a direct edit is reverted by the next deploy. Full steps in <5>docs/runbooks/enable_role_matching.md</5>.

plan.weDonTKnowHow: We don't know how long this takes.
plan.notSomethingYouBuyThis: Not something you buy — this one is coached, practised and reviewed.

plan.pickARoleToAim: Pick a role to aim at
plan.reportedNeverSequencedThereS: Reported, never sequenced — there's no course for an over-expression and nothing here needs fixing.
plan.weDonTSetYou: We don't set you dated checkpoints. Nothing in your plan claims a deadline, and invented ones are something you'd end up measuring yourself against unfairly. Each step carries a review horizon instead — when it's worth looking at that one again.
plan.neverReachesPaybackAtThis: never reaches payback at this wage
plan.nearerTarget: There may be a nearer target
plan.areasThatSitNearerTo: Areas that sit nearer to you

plan.roiRefused: We can't work this out honestly yet. We'd rather show you nothing than a number we made up — you might make a real decision on it.
plan.workingOn: Working on {{what}}. It reads what the other steps found and takes a little while — long enough that we hand it off and come back for it. You can leave this page; it carries on without you.
plan.somethingBrokeOnOurSide: Something broke on our side part-way through. Nothing you've entered was lost, and running it again is safe.
plan.weVeLostTrackOf: We've lost track of that run
plan.thatJobIsnTThere: That job isn't there any more. Starting a fresh one costs you nothing but the wait.
plan.weCouldnTCheckWhether: We couldn't check whether you've already run this — that's a fault on our side, not a sign there's nothing here. Running it again is safe either way.
plan.thisOneIsComputedRather: This one is computed rather than stored, so it has to be asked for. You can run it whatever state the earlier steps are in — it will tell you what it was missing rather than pretend it wasn't.
plan.workingOutWhetherAMove: Working out whether a move pays off needs the side of the sum only you know. It is used for this calculation and nothing else.
plan.iMNotEarningAnything: I'm not earning anything at the moment

portrait.thisPageReadsBackWhat: This page reads back what your assessments, résumé and bio say about how you work. We don't have any of those on file yet, so there's nothing honest to show you here.
portrait.addingAnyOneOfThem: Adding any one of them is enough to get a first read — a résumé on its own produces a genuine portrait, just a less corroborated one.
portrait.weCouldnTPutYour: We couldn't put your portrait together just now. Refresh to try again — nothing you've added has been lost.
portrait.hereSWhatWeCan: Here's what we can see so far — how you tend to work, and what sits underneath that. It's a mirror to think with, not a verdict on you.
portrait.whatThisIsBuiltOn: What this is built on so far

rehearse.answerPlaceholder: Say it the way you'd actually say it — no need to polish.
rehearse.youCanSendThisBlank: You can send this blank. Drawing one is an answer too, and it gets a reply rather than a complaint.
rehearse.oneThingToTryNext: One thing to try next time
rehearse.sharingOn: On. A coach you work with can read these answers. Turn it off whenever you like.
rehearse.sharingOff: Off. Nobody else can see these answers — not a coach, not your employer.
rehearse.retention: Kept for {{days}} days after you last use it, then deleted on its own. Coming back to it starts that clock again.
rehearse.theQuestionsYourAnswersAnd: The questions, your answers and the feedback on them are removed — not hidden, not archived. Your journey still shows you did this step. There is no undo, which is the point.
rehearse.knowingWhatYouWantTo: Knowing what you want to say and being able to say it under mild pressure are two different skills. This step is for the second one — answering a few likely questions and getting a read on how the answer lands, in private, with nobody keeping score.
rehearse.plentyOfPeopleGoStraight: Plenty of people go straight from the prep sheet to the interview and do just fine. Skipping it doesn't leave a hole in anything.
rehearse.lookingForAnythingYouVe: Looking for anything you've already practised…
rehearse.weCouldnTLoadYour: We couldn't load your rehearsal just now. Refresh to try again — nothing you've answered has been lost.
rehearse.thatRehearsalIsnTThere: That rehearsal isn't there any more.
rehearse.itWasEitherDeletedOr: It was either deleted or it aged out. There's nothing to recover — and starting a new one takes a minute.
rehearse.noGuideOnFile: There is no interview guide on file yet, so there is nothing to rehearse against. Stage 11 builds one out of your own gaps against the role you are targeting.
rehearse.deletedYourAnswersAndThe: Deleted. Your answers and the feedback on them are gone.
rehearse.youLlGetAHandful: You'll get a handful of questions drawn from your own prep sheet, one at a time. Answer each one the way you'd actually say it, and you'll get a note back — what's there, and one thing to try next time. Nothing is scored, and you can stop after any question.
rehearse.thatSEveryQuestionIn: That's every question in this set.
rehearse.stopHereKeepWhatI: Stop here — keep what I've done
rehearse.stoppingCountsAsDoneThis: Stopping counts as done. This step can't be failed, and the ones you answered still count.
rehearse.answeredOfForRole: You answered {{answered}} of the {{total}} questions for {{role}}.

salary.unusableIncoherent: the reported figures don't line up.
salary.wedRatherShowNothing: We'd rather show you nothing than a number you can't check.
salary.shrinkingNotClosed: Shrinking is not the same as closed.
salary.noWageDataOnFile: No wage data on file for this occupation. That's a gap in what we hold, not a statement that the work pays nothing — we'd rather leave it blank than fill it with a stand-in figure.
salary.noEmploymentProjectionOnFile: No employment projection on file for this occupation.
salary.noWageDataAreaYet: No wage data on file for this career area yet.

salary.everyRangeWillSayWhere: Every range will say where it came from and when it was collected. If we can't tell you that, we won't show you the number.
salary.lookingUpWhatTheseAreas: Looking up what these areas pay…
salary.weCouldnTLoadThe: We couldn't load the pay data
salary.thatSAFaultOn: That's a fault on our side, not a sign there's nothing to show. Nothing you've done has been lost, and trying again is safe.

salary.theseArenTRankedFor: These aren't ranked for you yet — that needs a behavioural profile on file. They're still worth reading: this is what the work pays, whoever is looking.
